title: scw-florida-tag-team-titles-scw-entity-a

won.source: Already champions entering this document; no earlier document survives showing when the titles were won.

lost.source: Retained against The Warlords on this show; no later document survives.

note: Retained against The Warlords (Taurus and Irish Pride) on the CWF branch show, 9 August 1997.

title: scw-national-heavyweight-title-scw-entity-a
label: John Chapman

won.source: Won the vacant National Heavyweight Championship in an eight-man Tower of Doom cage match at the Continental Cup, escaping the cage floor first with an assist from a masked interferer.

note: Successfully defended the title to a time-limit draw against Chris Spencer on 11 April 1999 before losing it to him outright in a rematch billed "Chapman/Spencer II."

title: scw-national-heavyweight-title-scw-entity-a
label: Chris Spencer

won.source: Won the National Heavyweight Championship from John Chapman with a crossface submission as time expired on the promotion's own Homecoming 99 broadcast.

note: The promotion's own following pay-per-view, "One," staged a twenty-man battle royal for a future shot at this title rather than a direct defense; that match ended without a declared winner.

title: scw-television-title-scw-entity-a
label: "Ravishing" Ric Studd

won.source: Won the Television Championship from "Wild" David Carter on the promotion's own season-opening broadcast.

note: Defended successfully through at least early April 1999 per the promotion's own house-show line-ups; the title passed to The Carolina Crusher in a match not among the documents read for this record.

won.source: Won the vacant Television Championship in a Triple Threat Dog Collar match against "Mean" Mike McShane and "The Punisher" James Wilson at the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

title: scw-television-title-scw-entity-a
label: "Wild" David Carter

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Carter as the reigning Television Champion entering the 28 February 1999 broadcast, having won the title from Ric Studd before the record read for this wing begins.

note: Lost the title back to Ric Studd on the same broadcast where he disclosed a heart condition in a pre-match press conference.

title: scw-television-title-scw-entity-a
label: The Carolina Crusher

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing (an insider newsletter of 19 May 1999 names The Carolina Crusher as reigning Television Champion); the title-winning match itself is not among the documents read for this record.

note: Stripped of the title before the promotion's own first pay-per-view after the promotion judged the manner of the win illegitimate; the vacancy was filled that same night.

title: scw-television-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: The Westside Bulldogs

won.source: Won the Television Tag Team Championship from Gary Grace and The Carolina Crusher, aided by two masked interferers, on the promotion's own season-opening broadcast.

note: The title passed to the Playpen (Ike Harris and Lance Walker) before the promotion's own first pay-per-view, in a match not among the documents read for this record.

won.source: Won the Television Tag Team Championship from the Playpen, aided by a masked returnee later revealed as Logan Gunz, at the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

title: scw-television-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: Gary Grace and The Carolina Crusher

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Grace and The Carolina Crusher as the reigning Television Tag Team Champions entering the 28 February 1999 broadcast.

note: Lost the title to The Westside Bulldogs after two masked interferers turned the finish.

title: scw-television-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: The Playpen

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames the Playpen as the reigning Television Tag Team Champions entering the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

note: Lost the title to Marc LeRoux and Mikal Khastanovich, aided by a masked returnee, at the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

title: scw-tennessee-title-scw-entity-a
label: K-Fresh

won.source: Won the Tennessee Championship from Lance Love, aided by a run-in DDT from Ike Harris, on the promotion's own season-opening broadcast.

note: Defended successfully through at least early April 1999 per the promotion's own house-show line-ups; the title passed to "Panther" Jared Mathys in a match not among the documents read for this record.

title: scw-tennessee-title-scw-entity-a
label: Lance Love

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Love as the reigning Tennessee Champion entering the 28 February 1999 broadcast.

note: Lost the title to K-Fresh after a run-in DDT from Ike Harris.

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Mathys as the reigning Tennessee Champion entering the promotion's own Homecoming 99 broadcast of 16 May 1999.

title: scw-brass-knux-title-scw-entity-a
label: "Dynamite" Derek Sweger

won.source: Awarded the newly-created Brass Knux Championship in place of his retired Cruiserweight title by the promotion's own vice-president of operations.

note: Held up after the title's own first defense, against Chris Page, ended when both men were knocked unconscious falling through a table at the Continental Cup.

won.source: Won the Brass Knux Championship from Chris Page in a four-way Ambulance match against Page, The Phoenix and "Primetime" Brian Rich at the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

title: scw-brass-knux-title-scw-entity-a
label: "The American Rage" Chris Page

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Page as the reigning Brass Knux Champion entering the promotion's own first pay-per-view; the title-winning match itself is not among the documents read for this record.

note: Lost the title to Dan Starr in a four-way Ambulance match at the promotion's own first pay-per-view. A wrestler's own later vignette separately names himself a former Brass Knux Champion, suggesting a further, undated reign not otherwise attested in this record.

title: scw-southern-states-heavyweight-title-scw-entity-a
label: "The Iceman" David Smith

won.source: Won the Southern States Heavyweight Championship from Kenneth Karby III in a title-for-title Dog Collar match at the Continental Cup.

note: Defended successfully through at least mid-May 1999 per the promotion's own house-show line-ups.

title: scw-southern-states-heavyweight-title-scw-entity-a
label: Kenneth Karby III

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Karby as the reigning Southern States Heavyweight Champion entering the Continental Cup.

note: Lost the title, and a title-for-title stake against a rival promotion's own Florida title, to "The Iceman" David Smith in a Dog Collar match at the Continental Cup.

won.source: Won the vacant Southern States Tag Team Championship against Acid Rayne and Corruption and Violence in a three-way scaffold match at the promotion's own first pay-per-view, by tricking Sabbath into tagging in the wrong partner.

title: scw-southern-states-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: The Frasier Brothers

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames the Frasier Brothers as the reigning Southern States Tag Team Champions entering the Continental Cup.

note: The title fell vacant before the promotion's own first pay-per-view; the documents read for this record do not state the cause.

title: scw-national-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: Gary Grace and The Carolina Crusher

won.source: Won the newly-created National Tag Team Championship by winning the sixteen-team Continental Cup tag tournament, defeating Domination in the final.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own house-show line-up cards: the title passed to Corruption and Violence by 25 April 1999, then to the Frasier Brothers by the promotion's own first pay-per-view; neither transition is among the documents read for this record.

title: scw-national-tag-team-title-scw-entity-a
label: The Frasier Brothers

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames the Frasier Brothers as the reigning National Tag Team Champions entering the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

note: Retained the title by disqualification against Domination at the promotion's own first pay-per-view after an outside team attacked both sides.
